items.stem: A test is flaky because an element appears slightly late. What is the idiomatic Playwright fix?

options.text: Rely on auto-waiting via a web-first assertion like expect(locator).toBeVisible()
options.rationale: Correct: Playwright auto-waits and retries the assertion until it passes or times out.
Fixed sleeps are brittle and slow; they hide rather than fix the race.
Disabling retries does not address the timing issue.

options.text: Switch to a brittle nth-child CSS selector
options.rationale: Brittle selectors increase flakiness, not reduce it.

items.explanation: Correct: Playwright auto-waits and retries the assertion until it passes or times out.

items.stem: Which TWO practices make a Playwright suite faster and more reliable? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Reusing a saved authentication storage state across tests
options.rationale: Correct: reusing auth state avoids logging in through the UI every test.
Correct: accessible-role locators are more resilient than brittle CSS.

options.text: Sharing mutable global state between parallel workers
options.rationale: Shared mutable state across workers causes flakiness.
Fixed sleeps slow the suite and mask real timing issues.

items.stem: What does the Playwright trace viewer primarily help you do?

options.text: Inspect a timeline of actions, DOM snapshots and network to diagnose a failure
options.rationale: Correct: the trace viewer reconstructs what happened during the run.
The trace viewer inspects; it does not rewrite code.

options.text: Guarantee a test can never be flaky again
options.rationale: It aids diagnosis but offers no such guarantee.
Assertions remain essential; the trace only helps debugging.
